entries.title: Add several PDF or HTML files at once
entries.body: Choose or drop two or more PDF or HTML files and they are added together, with a panel to stop the batch or retry a single file. Files already in your library are skipped, and if you reach your allowance the rest of the batch stops. Each one arrives marked Not AI-processed yet, with its title, authors, abstract and DOI, and for a PDF the file itself. Nothing more is done with it until you press Read this.

entries.title: Structure can show the whole outline at once
entries.body: Structure mode has a second view, Expanded, beside the usual Fisheye: every part and section at any depth, each with its summary, in one scrolling list that moves with you when you read into another section. The arrow keys also behave the same everywhere: Up and Down step one paragraph at a time, except over the strip showing where you are in the article, and with Structure open, Left and Right step between the smallest sections.

entries.title: Investigate in Citations is renamed Dig deeper
entries.body: In Citations, the button beside each cited work is renamed Dig deeper. Every press searches the web first, which you see as it happens, and the answer comes from a stronger AI with more room before it is cut off. Results from the old Investigate button no longer show; press Dig deeper for a fresh one.

entries.title: Summary keeps to its three levels
entries.body: Summary mode drops its outline of parts and sections, which repeated Structure, and keeps the Brief, Simple and Fuller summaries, with a button at each end of the slider, in a slightly wider panel. Newly made summaries and Tweets threads leave out authors, funding, acknowledgements and similar paperwork unless the piece uses them, and end on its conclusion.

entries.title: Trajectory is renamed Skim, among smaller changes
entries.body: Trajectory is called Skim, and old links still open it; its stop cards no longer show FAQ questions. Chat is told which passages were on your screen when you asked. Sketch's wait message says about a minute. Glossary terms have a heavier dotted underline than cross-references, and the reading-time line in the margin explains itself when you point at it.

entries.title: Past imports show more; Metadata page has search
entries.body: On the add page, past imports show their source and time, and a failed one has a Report this button. The box for why you are reading shows whether it saved; leave it empty and the article asks once when it opens. On the Metadata page, contents open the section you pick and a search finds sections by topic.

entries.title: Fewer gaps and failures adding PDFs and books
entries.body: A PDF's tables could show only a caption over an empty box, and figures made of several panels could be missing; both appear, for PDFs added from now on. Long documents such as books could fail while building their levels of detail; small faults are repaired where possible, or the AI is asked once more.

entries.title: Dictation follows your computer's microphone setting
entries.body: In Chrome and browsers built on it, dictation and Live conversation with no microphone picked could listen to the browser's own default instead of the one your computer uses, and hear nothing. They follow your computer's setting, the dictation strip names the microphone in use while dictation is on, and the first choice in the list is called System default.
